name: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego
role: Daniel's three friends, thrown into the furnace
whenBasis: Taken to Babylon with Daniel in the third year of Jehoiakim (Daniel 1:1), ≈605 BC, and serving Nebuchadnezzar, who reigned until 562 BC. Daniel does not date the furnace.
summary: Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, young men of Judah taken to Babylon with Daniel and given the Babylonian names Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. With Daniel they kept from the king's food and were found ten times wiser than the king's magicians. Set over the province of Babylon, they refused to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue and were thrown bound into a furnace heated seven times hotter. The king saw four men walking unharmed in the fire, called them out, and blessed their God.
body: Their answer to the king is the heart of the story: their God is able to deliver them, “But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.” The men who threw them in are killed by the flames; the three come out without even the smell of fire on them.
When Nebuchadnezzar dreams of the great statue, Daniel asks his three friends to plead with the God of heaven for mercy. They are not mentioned after chapter 3.

later.text: The Greek text of Daniel adds the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Young Men, sung in the furnace. They are in the Catholic and Orthodox Bibles and the Protestant Apocrypha.

sources.title: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three Young Men (Greek Daniel 3:24–90)

later.text: The Talmud says they are not mentioned again because they went up to the land of Israel.
